The conventional cryo-EM computational pipeline first combines many particle images to reconstruct an electrostatic potential (ESP) map and then fits an atomic model to the recovered map. Density reconstruction has high sample complexity, requiring large numbers of particle images and making structure determination high-cost and low-throughput, particularly for heterogeneous samples. Downstream atomic model building, in turn, becomes increasingly difficult as the resolution of the reconstructed map deteriorates. Protein structure prediction models provide strong sequence-derived priors on atomic structure, and experiment-guided approaches can use these priors to recover structures consistent with experimental measurements. Yet, in cryo-EM, such priors are typically integrated only after density reconstruction during atomic model fitting. We introduce Fold'EM, an inference-time framework that combines priors from protein generative models directly with cryo-EM particle images to determine atomic models from a small number of single particle images, bypassing both intermediate density reconstruction and downstream model building against the reconstructed map. Across synthetic and experimental cryo-EM datasets, Fold'EM recovers accurate atomic structures both with known particle orientations and in an ab-initio setting where orientations are inferred jointly with structure. In heterogeneous datasets, Fold'EM further resolves distinct conformational states from mixed particle populations without separately reconstructing a density map and building an atomic model for each state. We believe these results open new avenues for structure determination in the low-sample regime and for characterizing low-population conformational states directly from cryo-EM particles.

title: TRACE: Trajectory Return Attribution and Contrastive Erasure for Multi-Turn Safety
abstract: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) often refuse a harmful request but comply once the same goal is spread over several turns. Preference objectives score whole responses to single prompts, so their training loss alone cannot control risk on unseen histories. Our analysis gives sufficient conditions under which suppression at supervised single-turn contexts yields a bound on multi-turn trajectory risk. The bound accounts for coverage, transfer slack, and leakage, and characterizes contraction relative to a base-policy risk budget evaluated on the trained policy's contexts. TRACE (Trajectory Return Attribution and Contrastive Erasure) turns this principle into a token-level objective. On the safe response, each token is weighted by the discounted return of a refusal-attributable advantage. The advantage compares a frozen reference model with its refusal-ablated copy, allowing earlier response tokens to receive credit from later refusal-related evidence. At high-gap positions on rejected responses, TRACE combines the observed token with policy-selected alternatives in the erasure target. A gradient-norm penalty replaces the retain set. Across five open-weight models and seven multi-turn attacks, TRACE gives the lowest attack success rate (ASR) in all 35 model and attack pairs, while the model utility evaluated on MMLU and HellaSwag drop by at most 1\.23 points. Source code can be found in the supplemental material.

title: Robustness of the Verwey transition against remanent strain-induced defects in magnetite
abstract: The Verwey transition in magnetite is a benchmark electronically driven phase transition that is highly sensitive to lattice imperfections and external perturbations. Doping, deviations from oxygen stoichiometry, and irradiation-induced point defects are known to lower the Verwey transition temperature, $T_{\rm V}$. By contrast, the role of remanent strain fields and extended defect structures generated by uniaxial stress has remained largely unexplored. Here we combine dark-field x-ray microscopy (DFXM) and ac magnetic susceptibility to determine how strain-induced defects affect the Verwey transition in stoichiometric single-crystalline magnetite after uniaxial compression and unloading. The DFXM measurements were performed on two samples compressed along the same $[011]$ direction: loading to $200~\mathrm{MPa}$ generated stable line-like defects and remanent strain fields, whereas loading beyond the fracture threshold produced denser defect networks and mechanical fracture. To test the effect of a different loading geometry, we also measured the ac susceptibility of a sample fractured by compression along $[001]$. Real-space DFXM imaging, lattice-orientation mapping, and residual strain mapping show substantial remanent structural disorder after compression. Nevertheless, neither the transition temperature $T_{\rm V}$ nor the sharpness of the transition changes measurably in any of the compressed or fractured samples. This behavior contrasts with the strong suppression of $T_{\rm V}$ by point-like disorder. Our results show that extended line-like defects and remanent strain fields produced by plastic deformation do not measurably perturb the macroscopic electronic ordering responsible for the Verwey transition, thereby distinguishing the effects of point defects from those of extended slip-related defects in magnetite.

title: EP-Flow: Disordered Crystal Structure Prediction without Site-Level Annotations
abstract: Generative models have made rapid progress in ordered crystal structure prediction, yet many functional materials are intrinsically disordered, with substitutional mixing, vacancies, or interstitial species controlling their properties. Existing crystal generators either assume deterministic site occupations or require site-level disorder annotations, which are often unavailable when the chemical formula is the primary input. We formulate disordered crystal structure prediction through an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM), a continuous site-by-species representation that unifies ordered crystals, solid solutions, vacancy disorder, and interstitial occupancy. A valid ODM must satisfy coupled site-wise occupancy, mass-conservation, and non-negativity constraints, placing each sample on a formula-dependent transportation polytope. We propose Entropic Polytope Flow (EP-Flow), a marginal-constrained flow matching framework that canonicalizes heterogeneous polytopes into a shared double-centered space, learns a marginal-preserving flow, and recovers feasible occupancies through a Sinkhorn inverse map. By jointly generating occupancies, fractional coordinates, and lattice parameters, EP-Flow achieves state-of-the-art performance on formula-conditioned disordered CSP benchmarks derived from COD and MPDS, substantially outperforming adapted ordered-crystal generators. Analyses further show that EP-Flow recovers sparse and chemically meaningful local disorder patterns rather than merely matching global composition statistics.

title: Functionalized WS2 Electronic Nose for Volatile Organic Compound Mixture Recognition via Chemically Informed Transformer Learning
abstract: Accurate detection and discrimination of volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in complex environments using chemiresistive sensors remains a major challenge, mainly due to overlapping responses (cross-sensitivity) and environmental interferences. In this study, we have developed a sensor array based on defect-engineered, tungsten disulfide (WS2) nanosheets chemically functionalized with organic ligands for the detection of oxygenated VOCs.

title: Accelerating Identification of Relevant Polarons in Batteries
abstract: Many of the materials under consideration as battery electrodes are known to exhibit polarons─charge carriers localized through polarizing their environments, which are unfortunately quite costly to tackle by theory. Next to costly ab initio methods and geometry optimizations, the main problem is the sheer number of possible configurations polarons can adopt in a material. This problem is exacerbated by symmetry-breaking defects such as oxygen vacancies ubiquitous in oxide materials. Fortunately, a majority of polaron configurations tend to be too high in energy to ever be adopted at normal operating temperatures. In this work, we therefore present a data-driven approach based on gradient-boosted decision trees as a descriptor for relative polaron energies. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach to weed out those configurations that are energetically unlikely in three simulation cells of defected spinel Lithium4Titanium5Oxygen12 (LTO). The first two cells differ by their 16d-site occupational disorder and the position of the oxygen vacancy, which in both cases leads to the formation of two polarons in the cells. In contrast, the third simulation cell contains an extra lithium ion, which leads to three polarons. Our approach allows us to reduce the number of necessary first-principles calculations by roughly two-thirds. It can easily be adapted to other materials and simulation cells, greatly speeding up their theoretical treatment.

title: Models building models for discovery of graphene metamaterial design principles in the context of failure
abstract: Artificial intelligence assists scientific discovery, but most agents operate previously developed instruments. Whether an agent can build an instrument, translating physical theory into reliable measurements and testable predictions, then use it for open-ended research remains open. Here, from a single prompt, an AI agent built and validated an atomistic simulator and conducted 96 simulations across ten graphene architecture families. At matched mass, load paths governed strength, and tilted slits revealed distinct failure mechanisms.

title: DrugForge-ADMET v0.3.0: An auditable BRICS-based workflow
abstract: Early hit discovery normally begins with a physical or virtual collection of small molecules. Public resources such as PubChem, ChEMBL and ZINC have broadened access to chemical space, but using them effectively still requires retrieval, standardization, filtering, deduplication, three-dimensional preparation and provenance management; many laboratories also lack an in-house screening collection. We present DrugForge-ADMET v0.3.0, an open-source RDKit workflow intended to provide a compact, auditable starting set when a prepared library is unavailable.

title: Reductive insertion of a trivalent metal leading to the isolation of Prussian blue-type EuIIIFe3[Fe(CN)6]3
abstract: Reductive insertion reactions selectively modify three-dimensionally bonded solid-state structures through the addition of an elemental metal by electronation of the host structure and insertion of the metal cation into the host cavities for charge balance. However, with rare exceptions, this class of reactions has been largely restricted to insertions of monovalent metals.

title: Scoring close linker analogues in PROTAC ternary complexes: A matched-pose study of VHL-recruiting SHP2 degraders
abstract: Linker optimisation in targeted protein degradation remains largely empirical, and a computational method able to rank close analogues before synthesis would be valuable. Whether current methods can do so has not been tested against the smallest chemical difference that changes potency. Here two VHL-recruiting SHP2 degraders that differ by exactly one methylene, P9 and P10, were compared across 27 ternary complex arrangements generated for both compounds, so that in every comparison the protein–protein geometry was held fixed and only the degrader varied.

title: All-Optical Spin Coherence in a Photosynthetic Electron-Transfer Metalloprotein
abstract: Optically addressable, biocompatible spin qubits represent promising platforms for quantum sensing. However, current efforts have focused on genetic encodability and microwave-based approaches thus far limited to organic radicals. Utilizing time-resolved Faraday rotation, we measured electron spin coherence in plastocyanin, a protein in the photosynthetic electron transport chain. Persisting hundreds of picoseconds, this is the first measurement of spin coherence in a metalloprotein under ambient conditions.

title: LipidOracle: Ambiguity-aware lipid annotation across fragmentation methods
abstract: Tandem mass spectra (MS²) rarely determine a complete lipid structure, yet annotation software reports a best-scoring name and leaves users to judge whether the spectrum distinguishes it from other isomers. LipidOracle enumerates every isomer compatible with a precursor, converts the scores into probabilities with a softmax calibrated on standards, and reports the structural detail on which the credible candidates agree. An independent audit tests whether any observed fragment separates the reported structure from its closest rival.

title: Thermal pathway reconstruction exposes a reliability gap for AI-guided materials design
abstract: AI-guided materials design increasingly connects candidate generation with processing and experimental planning, yet recognizing a material’s final thermal endpoint is not the same as reconstructing how it gets there. We benchmarked closed-book reconstruction of source-qualified differential scanning calorimetry event maps for 30 molecular materials using GPT-5.6 Luna, GPT-6 Luna, GPT-5.6 Sol, and Claude Opus 5.5. In the primary API experiment, models recovered terminal melting in 194/216 opportunities (89.8%) but other thermal transitions and pathways in only 105/318 (33.0%).

title: Mapping under-represented chalcone chemical space with an open-source Virtual Chalcone Library (VCL)
abstract: Chalcones are highly versatile privileged scaffolds, yet substantial regions of their synthetically accessible chemical space remain under-explored. Herein, we report an open-source Virtual Chalcone Library (VCL) comprising 489,475 unique structures generated from commercially available aromatic ketones and aldehydes using the freely available DataWarrior platform. Comparison of the VCL with a curated dataset of 8,886 literature chalcones revealed structural bias towards a small number of pharmacophore motifs, while highlighting under-represented regions of chemical space.

title: Compositional flexibility and structure dynamics of Strätlingite
abstract: Strätlingite, Ca 2 Al(AlSi)O 2 (OH) 10 ·2.25H 2 O a phyllosilicate found in nature and in ancient Roman concrete, was investigated for its synthesis conditions, phase stability, and thermal and chemical degradation mechanisms. Contrary to previous reports, phase formation was observed to be complete after ~3 days of setting, using hand-ground precursors, while the applied water:solid ratio has only minimal effect on purity of the resulting strätlingite.

title: Donor–Acceptor Integration Modulates Reverse Intersystem Crossing in Multi-Resonant TADF Emitters
abstract: Multi-resonant thermally activated delayed fluorescent (MR-TADF) compounds are attractive as emitters in organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) owing to their high photoluminescence quantum yields and narrowband emission. However, these emitters generally have moderate reverse intersystem crossing rate constants (kRISC), which causes triplet exciton accumulation and leads to, amongst other excitonic processes, triplet-triplet annihilation. This process results in significant efficiency roll-off in OLEDs at high luminance.

title: Low-Cost, Home Synthesis of Vaterite: A Factorial Study of Calcium Source, Temperature, Citric Acid Modification, and Mixing Intensity
abstract: This paper presents a low cost, home-accessible method for synthesizing vaterite-type calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) using consumer-available materials and simple household tools. Vaterite is a metastable CaCO₃ polymorph of interest for biomedical, filler, and coating applications, but existing synthesis protocols typically require laboratory-grade reagents and equipment, limiting accessibility for independent researchers. The two required precursors, sodium carbonate (from baking soda) and calcium acetate (from eggshells and vinegar), were prepared in house.

title: Rate-independent limits on a sulphating, self-renewing oxide catalyst: exact master-equation results with lattice kinetic Monte Carlo checks
abstract: Copper oxide takes up sulphur dioxide as a sorbent because sulphation converts it to inactive copper sulphate. Whether a copper oxide surface that sulphates in service and renews itself by exposing fresh copper can instead act as a catalyst for SO 2 oxidation is a question about site statistics as much as chemistry. We study it with a lattice model whose elementary rates are unknown, and we therefore restrict the main claims to statements that hold for every strictly positive assignment of rate constants. Three such results are established.

title: Biomimetic remodelling of lipid membranes using DNA nanostructures
abstract: The remodelling of biological membranes underpins a diverse range of sophisticated cellular processes, from cell crawling to mitosis to pathogen infection cycles. A refined understanding of the biophysical principles governing lipid bilayer remodelling is necessary to engineer ever-more advanced behaviours in microrobots, like synthetic cells, with disruptive applications in both fundamental biology and advanced biotechnology.

title: Evolutionary Design for Anion-Derived Interphase Stability
abstract: High-concentration electrolytes (HCEs) improve lithium-ion battery cycling by shifting interphase formation from the solvent to the anion, producing a more stable inorganic-rich interphase at the anode. However, the anions for HCEs has been mainly studied on FSI− and TFSI−, and the anion itself has received little systematic exploration relative to the solvent and the salt concentration. Here, anion chemical space is searched using evolutionary framework that couples genetic algorithm with quantum-chemical descriptors of reducibility, solvent coordination, and charge delocalization.

title: Asymmetric selectivity at the glycoprotein hormone receptor allosteric site
abstract: Position 7.42 of the glycoprotein hormone receptors has been proposed as the determinant of mutual selectivity between LHCGR and FSHR, but has not been tested reciprocally. We compared the allosteric pockets of LHCGR with Org 43553 (PDB 7FIH) and FSHR with Cpd-21f (PDB 8I2G), and mapped each ligand into the other receptor by transmembrane superposition. Seven of 27 aligned contact positions diverge, a rate not distinguishable from the transmembrane background, and the mapping is markedly asymmetric.

title: Design Rules for Mixed Rutile PGM Oxides
abstract: Oxide solid solutions have important industrial applications including catal-ysis that require high stability under operating conditions. The stability of solid solutions is usually predicted using structural similarity, with low lattice mismatch resulting in stable solid solutions and high lattice mismatch resulting in unstable solid solutions. While this works for most solid solutions, some such as yttria-stabilised zirconia break the rules and remain stable due to other factors.

title: Oxidative strong metal-support interaction determines selectivity in supported Rh catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation
abstract: The restructuring of a catalyst’s interface with its support can be tailored via strong metal-support interactions (SMSI) in order to achieve desired product selectivity. SMSI is usually associated with reductive conditions, where a reduced oxide support covers a supported metal phase and alters catalytic activity. Here, pretreatment-dependent SMSI of rhodium nanoparticles supported on rutile titania is shown to control the selectivity profile for CO 2 hydrogenation reactions between methanation and the reverse water-gas shift reaction at 500 °C.

title: Probing Nanoscale Carrier Dynamics in P3HT Blended with a Non-Fullerene Acceptor: Impact of Mixing on Device-Relevant Carrier Generation
abstract: High-performing organic photovoltaics (OPVs) rely not only on the appropriate energetics and interfaces for separating excitons into charges, but on distinct areas of donor-rich and acceptor-rich domains to transport those charges to electrodes once separated. In this work, we study a bulk heterojunction (BHJ) of well-studied poly(3-hexylthiophene-2,5-diyl) (P3HT) and a non-fullerene acceptor with an A1-D-A2-D-A1 motif, octyl rhodanine-thiophene-benzothiadiazole-thiophene-octyl rhodanine (ORTBT).

title: Parameter Recovery and Noise Sensitivity of Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Michaelis–Menten Kinetics: A Benchmark Against Classical Nonlinear Least Squares
abstract: This study evaluates a physics-informed neural network (PINN) for estimating Michaelis–Menten kinetic parameters from sparse and noisy concentration–time observations. The investigated system follows the ordinary differential equation , with a true maximum reaction rate of , Michaelis constant , initial substrate concentration , and a simulation duration of 10 time units. Synthetic observations were generated using numerical integration and additive Gaussian noise at 1% and 5% levels.

title: In situ Activation of Ni(II) with Boronic Acids and Application of a Phosphasilinane Ligand enable the Suzuki-Miyaura Cross-Coupling of Deactivated (Hetero)Aryl Chlorides
abstract: The important substitution of costly palladium catalysts with earth-abundant nickel alternatives in Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reactions is still problematic for challenging substrates, such as heteroaryls and (hetero)aryl chlorides. In this context, we report the application of low Vbur and electron-rich biaryl-based phosphasilinane ligands in nickel-catalyzed Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling reaction of electron-rich (hetero)aryl-chlorides with aryl boronic acid substrates, at catalyst loadings as low as 0.5 mol-% on gram-scale synthesis.

title: A numerically verified analytical framework for immobilised-enzyme packed-bed reactor design in the kinetically controlled regime applied to dihydroxyacetone production
abstract: Continuous-flow biocatalysis can decouple enzymatic productivity from the cellular growth constraints inherent to fermentation, but exploiting this advantage requires a reactor design framework that links enzyme kinetics, immobilisation penalties, and catalyst deactivation to industrially relevant performance metrics. We develop an analytical quasi-steady-state (QSS) plug-flow reactor model for immobilised-enzyme packed-bed reactors (PBRs) operating under first-order catalyst deactivation, and verify its transport assumptions against a two-dimensional axisymmetric COMSOL™ finiteelement model.

title: Direct Asymmetric Hydroalkoxylation of Styrenes Through Flavin Brønsted Acid Biocatalysis
abstract: Direct addition of free alcohols across alkenes would provide a concise route to chiral ethers, but controlling alkene activation, nucleophile capture, and stereochemistry remains difficult. We evolved an oleate hydratase, an enzyme that naturally adds water across alkenes, to favor alcohol addition instead. The resulting enzyme catalyzes intermolecular hydroalkoxylation of electron-rich styrenes in aqueous solution, reaching up to 80% yield and >99% enantiomeric excess.

title: On the enzymatic synthesis of ketone-containing oligomers and their processing into sustainable crosslinked materials
abstract: In this work, two ketone-containing pre-polyesters based on dimethyl 2-oxoglutarate (pDMOG) and dimethyl 1,3-acetonedicarboxylate (pDADC), were obtained via a solventless polymerization reaction in presence of Lipase B from Candida antarctica as the biocatalyst. 1 H-NMR indicated diol conversions over 90% for both monomers, while GPC analysis revealed differences between the two systems, with pDMOG reaching a M n of ≈ 8 kDa ( M w ≈ 30kDa) while pDADC reached a M n of ≈1.5 kDa ( M w ≈ 2.5 kDa).

title: Probing Oxygen Transport in β-Cyclodextrin–Cyclohexane Crystal Nanochannels by Luminescence Quenching from Nanoseconds to Seconds
abstract: Molecular transport in nanochannels can deviate from normal diffusion and exhibit different regimes depending on the observation timescale. However, resolving them from nanoseconds to seconds remains challenging. Here, oxygen transport in β -cyclodextrin–cyclohexane supramolecular crystals containing solvent-filled nanochannels is probed using room-temperature phosphorescence and fluorescence of aromatic luminophores. Their emission lifetimes, ranging from approximately 50 ns to 15 s, provide intrinsic time windows spanning more than eight orders of magnitude.

title: Two barriers to benchmarking structure-based virtual screening against the AcrB efflux pump: a sample-size ceiling and an identifiability failure
abstract: Background. The AcrAB-TolC system is the principal constitutive efflux pump of Escherichia coli and an attractive adjuvant target. Virtual screening campaigns against its distal binding pocket have been published without the retrospective validation standard elsewhere in the field. This study asked whether such a benchmark can be built from the published literature. Methods. Compounds reported as AcrB inhibitors were filtered against an independent reproducibility screen and assigned to a binding site by the strongest structural or mutational evidence available.

title: Project ⟨χ|χ⟩: Extending Dragonball towards Quantum Vibrational Spectroscopy
abstract: Semiclassical dynamics is able to add nuclear quantum effects to classical trajectories, in an approximate yet effective manner. However, moving from classical to semiclassical dynamics requires the careful consideration and implementation of many tools, especially in the case of ab initio semiclassical dynamics. In this paper, we present Project ⟨χ|χ⟩, a set of tools designed to extend the capability of the recently released Dragonball beyond quasi-classical trajectories. First, we improve Dragonball accessibility by providing a set of PySCF scripts to substitute ab initio software.

title: Distinguishing Pharmaceutical Salts and Cocrystals by Fluorescence Lifetime Mapping and Quantum Crystallography
abstract: Distinguishing between salt and cocrystal forms of a drug remains challenging in multicomponent systems with ambiguous proton transfer, particularly during bulk production in the pharmaceutical industry. Here, we address this challenge by combining fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) for rapid bulk-phase discrimination with Hirshfeld atom refinement (HAR) for single-crystal-level validation. This integrated FLIM–HAR approach was applied to 11 multicomponent solids derived from the pharmaceutical drugs niflumic acid, mefenamic acid, and sulfamethazine.

title: Insights into Electrolyte Effects on Interfacial Kinetics and Transport in Porous Redox Flow Battery Electrodes: A Multiparadigm Modelling Study
abstract: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising candidates for large-scale energy storage owing to their decoupled energy and power densities. Electrolyte formulation plays a key role in determining the electrochemical performance of RFBs, influencing interfacial kinetics and transport within porous electrodes. Herein, we develop a multiscale modelling framework to investigate the coupled effects of the electrolyte concentration (Methyl Viologen (MV) and NaCl) and the fibrous 3D microstructure on the porous transport and electrochemical kinetics in organic RFBs using a kinetic Monte…

title: Multigram Copper-Catalyzed Azidodeboronation of Alkenyl Boronates
abstract: A multigram synthetic approach to alkenyl azides based on copper-catalyzed azidodeboronation of alkenyl pinacol boronates was described. The optimized protocol relied on the use of Cu(OAc) 2 as the reaction promoter, which provided higher, reproducible yields and did not cause uncontrolled decomposition of the reaction mixture, unlike the CuSO 4 ·5H 2 O-based protocol reported previously. The method was applicable to β-, β,β-, and α,β-substituted substrates, including those bearing electron-withdrawing groups and saturated O -, N -, and S -heterocyclic motifs.

title: Redox-Paired Activation of Sulfur Hexafluoride Enables Nucleophilic C(sp3)–F Bond Formation
abstract: Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) is a potent greenhouse gas whose direct use as a fluorine source in organic synthesis remains underdeveloped. Here, we disclose complementary photoredox and electrochemical strategies for nucleophilic fluorinations with SF6, merging oxidative formation of carbocation intermediated from alkoxamines, carboxylic acids, or thiols with SF6 reduction, the latter providing fluoride for C(sp3)–F bond formation.

title: Majority-Rule of Enantiomeric Excess in Chiral Halide Perovskites for continuous tuning of chiroptical properties
abstract: Chiral halide perovskites have emerged as a promising platform for spin-optoelectronic applications, yet the role of chiral precursor composition in governing their chiroptical properties remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how enantiomeric excess (ee) controls the chiroptical response of the prototypical two-dimensional (2D) chiral halide perovskite (R/S-MBA)2PbI4 (MBA = methylbenzylammonium) across a compositional series spanning ee = −100% to +100%, corresponding to R-MBA mole fractions ranging from 0% to 100%.

title: Analysis of fine-tuned foundation interatomic potentials and their knowledge distillation into a cluster expansion for Ni–Pt ordering thermodynamics
abstract: Predicting alloy ordering thermodynamics requires the energies of thousands of atomic arrangements at fixed composition, far more than density functional theory (DFT) can routinely provide. Fine-tuned foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are a promising alternative, but whether they resolve the small energy differences between arrangements has not been established. Here, we examine this for fcc Ni–Pt in three steps. First, six foundation MLIPs fine-tuned on the same DFT data are evaluated on a 64-structure DFT benchmark.

title: Ultramild conversion of nitrobenzene to aniline mediated by metal organic alloy NiGraf in green solvent
abstract: The conversion of nitrobenzene to aniline can be carried out under ultramild conditions (35 °C under N2 at ambient pressure) with a 40% molar excess of hydrazine as reducing agent mediated by metal-organic alloy NiGraf in aqueous tetrahydrofuran, a green solvent. Conversion of nitrobenzene to aniline will optimally employ the stable and recyclable form of the NiGraf, consisting of reduced graphene oxide entrapped in jamborite nanoparticles, in renewable solvent system H2O/THF.

title: Acyl-1,4-Dihydropyridines as Efficient Dual-Mode Photoinitiators for Radical Polymerisation under Blue and Green Light
The Critical Role of Water in Safe, Scalable Diboron-Mediated Nitro Reductions .
abstract: The use of diboron compounds for nitro group reduction, an essential transformation in the synthesis of a wide range of nitrogen-containing functional groups, offers an attractive alternative to traditional methods like hydrogenation and dissolving metal reduction. This method has seen limited uptake in the literature despite avoiding transition metals and specialized equipment.

title: Nucleotide-mediated catalytic peptide synthesis from aminonitriles
abstract: Aminonitriles are accessible from simple feedstock compounds and their hydrolysis offers an abiotic route to life’s amino acids on the early earth. However, controlled aqueous polymerisation of amino acids into peptides remains challenging. Here we show that peptides can be directly generated and elongated by aminonitriles when the latter are coupled to nucleotides as a phosphoramidate. Upon thiol catalysis and pH shifts, a series of selective reactivities drives iterative peptide bond formation in water.

title: Piezoelectricity-Induced Mechanical Bond Formation in Solid-state Using Mechanochemistry
abstract: Mechanochemistry, long promoted as a sustainable route to chemical synthesis, remains difficult to apply predictably to complex reactions due to a limited atomic-level understanding of how mechanical energy drives reactivity. Here, we demonstrated how piezoelectric polarization in tetragonal BaTiO3 directs solid-state mechanoredox chemistry, enabling electrode-free, reductant-free and solvent-free synthesis, for forming complex mechanically interlocked molecules for the first time.

title: Iterative Multimutant Design Creates a Family-Like Enzyme Ensemble
abstract: Natural enzyme families achieve functional breadth by diversifying a common scaffold into specialized enzymes. Engineering comparable family-like diversity for synthetic chemistry is challenging because directed evolution workflows frequently optimize one enzyme for one substrate at a time. Here we show that an iterative process of designing and screening energetically compatible multimutant variants can explore sequence space broadly and efficiently.

title: Mechanochemical conglomerate formation by ball milling - or not?
abstract: Inspired by a study reporting on the zinc oxide-induced mechanochemical conglomerate formation of racemic amino acids, we investigated the reaction behavior of the analogous 19F-labeled DL-valine. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy under magic-angle spinning (MAS) conditions was employed as the central analytical technique to analyze the reaction products. In contrast to our expectation, no conglomerate formation occurred, and in the presence of ZnO and methanol a polymeric complex with one zinc and two fluorinated valine molecules was formed in a vibrational ball mill.

title: Hyperfine dynamics as an internal control of reactive-oxygen-species output in a triplet-born flavin–superoxide radical pair
abstract: When reduced flavin is activated by molecular oxygen it forms a spin-correlated radical pair—a flavin semiquinone and superoxide (O₂•⁻)—born in the triplet manifold, because ground-state O₂ is a triplet. Its singlet/triplet recombination gates the branching of reactive oxygen species, and the pair is realised in the electron-transfer flavoprotein, whose output is field-dependent. Radical-pair theory almost always treats the hyperfine tensor as fixed and the field as the variable.

title: Enhanced Catalysis via Multiscale Force Propagation in All-Enzyme Glucose Oxidase Hydrogels
abstract: Enzyme-based biomaterials are sustainable catalytic platforms with applications in biosensing, pharmaceutical synthesis, and environmental remediation. A key challenge is developing universal immobilisation strategies that preserve activity without requiring enzyme-specific optimisation. One promising approach is the photochemical cross-linking of native tyrosine residues to form self-supporting all-enzyme hydrogels, where the enzyme serves as both the catalytic and structural component.

title: Evaluation of alternative polymerases for biocatalytic synthesis of modified oligonucleotides
abstract: Enzymatic synthesis of modified nucleic acids is gaining a lot of traction. Most approaches involve the combination of modified nucleoside triphosphates and engineered polymerases capable of accepting such altered substrates. Such enzymes are obtained through engineering campaigns based on directed evolution, positional saturation mutagenesis, and rational design approaches potentially guided by in silico methods. However, most polymerase evolution/design approaches rely on a restricted diversity of enzyme chassis.

title: Twenty Years of COF-1: The Spark That Launched a Field and Its Mysteries That Remain
abstract: COF-1, reported in 2005, was the first covalent organic framework (COF) and marked the birth of the field. Since then, COFs have quickly attracted attention by demonstrating how supramolecular chemistry and reticular design can be used to construct crystalline and porous organic frameworks with predictable molecularly defined pore sizes. More than two decades after its discovery, COF-1 remains one of the most studied COFs and has served as the gold standard for developing new methodologies and advances in COF crystallization.

title: Extracting Latent Sequence-Function Information from Directed Evolution to Design Improved C-H Azidases
abstract: Directed evolution is a powerful approach for enzyme engineering, but conventional workflows use only a fraction of the information generated during experimental screening. Typically, only top-performing variants are sequenced and propagated, while sequence-function information from the remainder of the library is discarded. Here, we develop a data-efficient strategy to recover and leverage this latent information for enzyme design.

title: Pore-Engineering Enhances Low-Temperature Mixed Ionic-Electronic Conduction in Two-Dimensional Polymer Lithium Ion-Battery Electrodes
abstract: Understanding the fundamental relationships between ionic and electronic charge transport in polymer systems is essential for the systematic development of bioelectronic, optoelectronic, and energy-storage devices that leverage these materials. A classic strategy to improve ionic conductivity in mixed conducting materials involves attaching ionophilic oligoethylene glycol (OEG) groups to charge-carrying polymers.

title: ADMET-Informed Machine Learning Prioritization of Hydrogel-Associated Compounds for Nanocarrier Evaluation
abstract: Experimental screening of large hydrogel-associated chemical collections is slow and resource-intensive. We developed an ADMET-informed machine-learning workflow for 2060 HydrogelDB-linked compounds, using the median of a separately reported admetSAR3.0 biodegradability-related output to define higher- and lower-score classes and the remaining 115 predicted ADMET properties as model inputs; preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, probability calibration, and threshold selection were confined to the training partitions of nested cross-validation.

title: Localized Sequential Backflow Ansatz for Scalable Neural Quantum States
abstract: Neural Quantum State Architectures have been shown to have high accuracy on a variety of molecular and lattice systems, often outperforming traditional methods. This work replaces the all-to-all paradigm of current neural quantum states with a localized recurrent sequential backflow mechanism. Results have empirically exhibited approximately quadratic wall-clock scaling over the system sizes tested, namely the hydrogen chain with atom with length of H 10 to H 400 , suggesting a viable path towards a scalable Neural Quantum State.

title: Bulk Post-Polymerization Modification of a Single-Crystalline 2D Polymer via the Katritzky Reaction: A Modular Platform for Functional 2D Materials
abstract: Synthesizing two-dimensional polymers (2DPs) via single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SCSC) topochemical polymerization presents a dual challenge: preorganizing multifunctional monomers into two-dimensional crystal lattices and ensuring their polymerizable groups remain in close proximity to enable topochemical reaction in 2D. Consequently, topochemical 2DPs remain rare, and strategies for their post-polymerization modification, a standard tool in 1D polymer chemistry, are even more limited.

title: IRexp: A database of experimental infrared band lists from open literature
abstract: IRexp is a collection of experimental infrared band lists (cm⁻¹ peak positions) mined from open chemistry literature, with author-reported ¹H/¹³C NMR strings and resolved structures where available. The research corpus holds 121,233 records from the PMC Open Access Subset and the Chemotion repository, including 57,646 structure-linked entries and 39,118 IR + ¹H + ¹³C + structure quadruples. The public dataset of record contains 88,519 CC-BY/CC0 records released under CC-BY-4.0, with ShareAlike and non-commercial records distributed separately under their source licences.

title: Heavy Metal-Binding Peptide Phytochelatin Drives Membraneless Compartmentalization and Biomineral-Like Structures via Nanoparticle Formation within Condensates
abstract: Phytochelatin is a heavy metal-binding biogenic peptide found across different organisms that helps cells mitigate cytotoxicity by chelating metal ions. Yeasts produce phytochelatin to chelate intracellular cadmium and sequester it as cadmium metal sulfide nanoparticles. These nanoparticles were proposed to be stored within cytoplasmic microcompartments, although it remains unclear whether they are stored within membrane-bound or membraneless compartments.

title: Surface functionalization of soft photocathodes with an azido-phosphonic acid monolayer for robust and efficient solar-to-H2 conversion
abstract: Organic semiconductors are promising candidates for light-assisted electrocatalysis but interfacial design remains a key challenge for improving performance and durability. Design guidelines include: i) appropriate matching of the catalyst Fermi level to the transport level of charges in the organic semiconductor under operando; ii) controlling surface hydrophilicity for rapid bubble-release in the hydrogen evolution reaction; and iii) retained operation in acidic and alkaline media.

title: An Algorithm for computing Three- and Four-Body Density Matrices from CASCI Wavefunction and AI-Assisted Code Optimization
abstract: Three- and four-body reduced density matrices in the active space are required for second-order n-electron valence perturbation theory (NEVPT2) following complete active-space configuration interaction (CASCI) calculations. We developed an algorithm to generate these computationally demanding quantities by extending the pi-CASCI program, which is based on the graphical symmetric group approach (GSGA). A manually written prototype was subsequently optimized through AI-assisted code optimization, resulting in substantially improved performance.

title: QMzyme: A Python Package for Automated and Systematic QM-based Enzyme Modeling
abstract: We introduce QMzyme, a Python package to automate the generation of Quantum mechanics (QM)-based enzyme models. QM calculations on enzymes are computationally challenging because full enzyme systems typically contain thousands of atoms, placing accurate QM treatments beyond practical computational limits.Therefore, QM-based enzyme studies rely on identifying a subset of atoms that captures the essential chemistry of the reaction environment, enabling tractable yet chemically meaningful calculations.

title: Ultrasound-assisted enzymatic synthesis of medium- and long-chain triacylglycerols from tricaprylin and algal oil
abstract: Medium and long-chain triacylglycerols (MLCTs) are functional lipids, but their efficient synthesis in various systems remains challenging. An ultrasound-assisted enzymatic interesterification process was developed using tricaprylin and algal oil as substrates. The optimized enzymatic conditions were obtained by artificial neural network modeling. The structure of enzyme and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of enzymatic process were both evaluated. The results showed that the MLCT yield reached 69.16%, with Cy-Cy-DHA as the predominant product (28.99%).

title: Enantio- and Regioselective Ni-Catalyzed Hydroarylation of Alkenes and Alkynes to Form C–N Axially Chiral Heterobiaryls
abstract: C–N axially chiral heterobiaryls are highly valuable yet synthetically challenging scaffolds. Atroposelective hydroarylation represents an ideal strategy for their construction, offering both high step- and atom-economy. Herein, we report an enantio- and regioselective Ni-catalyzed hydroarylation of unactivated alkenes for the efficient synthesis of C–N axially chiral heterobiaryls.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Predicting Chemical Stressor Effects on Conjugative Plasmid Transfer Rates Using Machine Learning
abstract: Chemical stressors in environmental and clinical settings can alter conjugative plasmid transfer, which is a key process driving antibiotic resistance dissemination. However, predicting these effects across chemically diverse compounds is challenging. Here, we compiled and curated data on the effect of chemical stressors on RP4 plasmid transfer, extracting compound identity, concentration, conjugation frequency, and experimental metadata from 73 in vitro studies.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastric Cancer: Diagnostic, Prognostic, and Predictive Developments, Evidence Maturity, and Translational Challenges
abstract: BackgroundGastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health burden characterized by substantial heterogeneity in diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), has been increasingly investigated for the analysis of endoscopic images, radiological scans, whole-slide pathology images, molecular profiles, liquid-biopsy data, and multimodal clinical datasets. This structured review summarizes recent AI-based developments in GC diagnosis, staging, prognostic assessment, and treatment-response prediction, with particular emphasis on the translational maturity of the available evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, Scopus, and Google Scholar were searched for relevant English-language publications from database inception through January 2026. Eligible studies were evaluated according to clinical task, data modality, model type, cohort size, study design, validation strategy, interpretability, clinical workflow readiness, and reported limitations.Recent findingsRecent AI models have demonstrated promising performance in selected research settings, particularly in endoscopic image analysis, computational pathology, CT-based radiomics, and multimodal prognostic modeling. However, most studies remain retrospective, single-center, and internally validated. Calibration, robustness, prospective clinical utility, and generalizability across populations and institutions remain insufficiently assessed. Major barriers to translation include data heterogeneity, annotation variability, overfitting, data leakage, external validation failure, algorithmic bias, regulatory requirements, reimbursement, clinician-AI interaction, medicolegal responsibility, post-deployment monitoring, and model drift.ConclusionAI has considerable potential to support GC diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning, but most current models remain insufficiently validated for routine clinical use. Future progress will depend on transparent reporting, standardized validation, multicenter prospective trials, clinically meaningful endpoints, and the integration of explainable, trustworthy AI systems into routine clinical workflows.

title: Capturing Spatial Covariance for Efficient Multipolar Electrostatic Parameterization in DNA via Multioutput Learning
abstract: In DNA force field development, introducing high-rank atomic multipole moments (AMMs) to describe electron cloud anisotropy improves the accuracy of electrostatic energy calculations. However, high-rank AMMs have many components. Existing machine learning methods usually model each component independently, which increases model size and computational cost. This approach ignores the correlations among components and cannot balance accuracy and efficiency.
venue: The journal of physical chemistry. B

title: Complex magnetic phase diagrams in Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ and Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$
abstract: We report the synthesis and comprehensive investigation of single-crystalline Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ and Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$, the first Ir-based members of the $Ln_2M$Al$_4$Ge$_2$ family. Both compounds crystallize in the tetragonal Tb$_2$NiAl$_4$Ge$_2$-type structure (space group $I4/mmm$) and exhibit easy-axis magnetic anisotropy with the crystallographic $c$ axis as the preferred magnetization direction. Tb$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N = 25$ K and develops a sequence of field-induced metamagnetic transitions accompanied by pronounced magnetotransport anomalies, including a nonlinear Hall response. In contrast, Er$_2$IrAl$_4$Ge$_2$ exhibits three successive zero-field magnetic transitions and a substantially richer low-temperature magnetic phase diagram comprising multiple competing field-induced phases confined to relatively modest magnetic fields. The differences between the Tb- and Er-based compounds demonstrate the wide range of magnetic behavior that can be realized within the \ce{Tb2NiAl4Ge2}-type structure. More broadly, the successful realization of Ir-based $Ln_2M$Al$_4$Ge$_2$ compounds considerably expands the accessible chemical space of this family and opens a route toward the exploration of related $4d$- and $5d$-based aluminogermanides.

title: Synthetic Priors for Real-World Detection: A Label-Free Framework for Identifying Ultra-Rare Objects
abstract: Detecting ultra-rare objects (frequency -6) without positive annotations remains a critical challenge in computer vision. We propose a Synthesis-Prior Driven paradigm that eliminates the need for real positive samples. Our core insight is that models trained on statistically and perceptually indistinguishable synthetic data can generalize effectively to real-world environments. To achieve this, we introduce a Differentiable Morphological Modeling framework, which embeds explicit physical and geometric priors into a differentiable synthesis engine.
venue: IEEE transactions on pattern analysis and machine intelligence

title: Improving Conversational Literature Retrieval Quality via Personalized Profile-Based Re-Ranking
abstract: Academic literature retrieval is constrained by the paradox of "information overload" versus "evidence scarcity", a tension that deepens when researchers iteratively refine their queries in multiturn conversational settings. To address this challenge, we propose Conversational Literature Personalized Reranking (CLPR), a personalized framework that unifies dense semantic retrieval with personalized user profiling.
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
